title: Backlog.save restores a disk answer onto a gate a run rewrote under the same id
goal: Backlog.save keeps an answer written to the file after load only on a gate the run left as loaded, so a gate the run reworded (new question or options under its id) gets no old answer back

run:
import sys, json, pathlib, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, '_tools')
import bl_base
r = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); d = r / bl_base.rel_dir(); d.mkdir(parents=True)
f = d / 'BG-aaaaaaaa.json'
gate = {"id": "g1", "kind": "provisional", "question": "old question", "options": ["a", "b"], "recommendation": "a"}
f.write_text(bl_base.canonical({"id": "BG-aaaaaaaa", "kind": "bug", "title": "t", "status": "todo", "gates": [gate]}), encoding='utf-8')
bl = bl_base.Backlog(r); it = bl.items['BG-aaaaaaaa']
disk = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding='utf-8')); disk['gates'][0].update(answer='a', by='operator')
f.write_text(bl_base.canonical(disk), encoding='utf-8')
it['gates'][0]['question'] = 'new question'; it['gates'][0]['options'] = ['x', 'y']; it['gates'][0]['recommendation'] = 'x'
bl.save(it)
g = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))['gates'][0]
ok = 'answer' not in g
print('reworded gate kept clean' if ok else 'old answer restored onto the reworded gate', g)
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

gates.question: How does Backlog.save decide a gate was left as loaded?
options: whole gate equals its loaded copy
question and options equal their loaded values
gates.recommendation: whole gate equals its loaded copy
gates.reason: matches the goal's wording, simplest, any run change to a gate keeps the run's version
gates.answer: whole gate equals its loaded copy

notes: Review gap of SP-moxpl354 (S4): no shipped command rewrites a gate under its id today, so the case is an edge. Order: BG-3pqzpd2q edits _tools/bl_base.py too, so it runs after this one.
